━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔗 INTERMARKET ANALYSIS: READING THE BIGGER PICTURE

Most retail traders focus only on price charts. Professional desks watch relationships between different markets to predict currency moves before they happen.

Intermarket analysis examines how bonds, commodities, and equities influence currency pairs. These correlations reveal institutional money flows and shift before retail notices.

REAL EXAMPLE — OCTOBER 2026:
When US 10-year Treasury yields spiked 15 basis points last Monday, USD/JPY rallied 80 pips within hours. Why? Higher yields attract foreign capital into dollar-denominated bonds, increasing dollar demand. Traders watching bond markets entered USD/JPY long before the breakout showed on charts.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS TO MONITOR:

- Gold vs USD Index: Inverse correlation. Gold weakness often signals dollar strength across majors like EUR/USD and GBP/USD
- Oil prices vs CAD: Canada is oil-exporter. Rising crude typically strengthens USD/CAD moves lower
- German Bund yields vs EUR: Higher eurozone yields support euro strength against low-yielders like CHF
- Risk sentiment via S&P futures: Risk-on strengthens AUD and NZD. Risk-off drives flows into JPY and CHF

HOW TO APPLY THIS:
Check bond yields and commodity prices before your forex session. If you see oil rallying but USD/CAD also rising, question the move. Divergences reveal weakness.

PRO TIP: Add US 10Y yields and DXY to your watchlist. When yields and dollar align directionally, major pairs like EUR/USD show cleaner trends with less chop.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📊 SESSION HIGHS & LOWS: YOUR INTRADAY ROADMAP

Session highs and lows are invisible support and resistance zones that smart money respects. These levels define where institutional flows reversed during specific trading sessions.

The forex market operates across three major sessions: Asian, London, and New York. Each session creates highs and lows that act as magnets for price during subsequent sessions.

REAL EXAMPLE — ASIAN SESSION:
GBP/USD set an Asian session high at 1.3142 early Wednesday morning. During London open, price pulled back then rejected perfectly off that level twice, giving a clean 35-pip scalp opportunity. Why? London traders saw overnight highs as resistance and sold into them.

HOW TO TRADE SESSION LEVELS:

- Mark previous session high/low on your chart daily
- Watch for rejections at these levels during overlap periods
- London/New York overlap especially respects Asian session boundaries
- Breaks of session highs with volume continuation often signal trend days

TIMEFRAME MATTERS:
On AUD/USD, if New York session closes at the high, Asian session often tests that level at open. Algorithms are programmed to retest key session levels. This creates repeatable setups.

EUR/CHF respects session lows religiously due to SNB intervention concerns. Traders avoid pushing through previous lows aggressively, creating bounce setups.

SMART MONEY RULE: When price breaks a session high during high-volume periods like London open or NFP release, the break usually extends 20-40 pips minimum. Trade the momentum, not the reversal.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 3 DAILY TRADING TIPS

1. WEDNESDAY VOLATILITY SETUP
Mid-week often brings range compression before Thursday economic data releases. On pairs like NZD/USD, consider tightening stops and reducing position size. Save capital for clearer Friday momentum.

2. CROSS PAIRS OFFER CLEANER TRENDS
Major pairs like EUR/USD are choppy lately due to conflicting central bank signals. Look at EUR/GBP or AUD/NZD instead. Cross pairs often trend cleaner when majors consolidate because they isolate relative strength between two non-dollar economies.

3. CHECK CORRELATION BEFORE DOUBLING EXPOSURE
If you are long both EUR/USD and GBP/USD, you essentially have double euro-zone exposure. These pairs move together 75 percent of the time. One losing trade is acceptable. Two correlated losers destroy accounts. Diversify your directional bias across uncorrelated pairs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚠️ RISK MANAGEMENT: DIVERSIFICATION DONE RIGHT

Diversification does not mean trading more pairs. It means spreading risk across uncorrelated positions so one bad trade does not wreck your week.

COMMON MISTAKE:
Trading USD/JPY, USD/CHF, and USD/CAD simultaneously. All three are dollar-based. If dollar sentiment shifts unexpectedly due to Fed speakers, all three positions move against you at once. That is concentration, not diversification.

PROPER FOREX DIVERSIFICATION:

- Mix currency exposure: Long EUR/USD and short AUD/JPY gives you euro and yen exposure without double dollar risk
- Vary session focus: Trade London volatility on GBP pairs, then switch to Asian session AUD or NZD setups
- Combine trend and range strategies: Trend-follow USD/CAD while range-trading EUR/GBP in consolidation

POSITION SIZING ACROSS PAIRS:
Never risk more than 6-8 percent total capital across all open positions. If you take three trades, that is roughly 2-2.5 percent risk each. This ensures no single correlation wipeout ends your month.

Real scenario: Last week a trader held long positions on both CHF/JPY and EUR/JPY. Both are yen-based. When Bank of Japan made hawkish comments, yen surged and both trades hit stops within minutes. Proper diversification would have limited exposure to yen direction.

FINAL RULE: Diversification protects against unknown unknowns. You cannot predict every central bank surprise or geopolitical headline. Spread your bets wisely.
